publications.title: Kandoo Car Credit Ltd enters administration
publications.summary: On 23 November 2026, Kandoo Car Credit Ltd (Kandoo) was placed into administration. Steve Kenny and Richard Cole of KBL Advisory Limited were appointed as joint administrators. Kandoo Car Credit (firm reference number 936619) operated as a motor finance credit broker arranging finance for consumers purchasing vehicles from third-party car dealerships. The joint administrators, Steve Kenny and Richard Cole of KBL Advisory Ltd, are now responsible for Kandoo while it is in administration. If you have questions about the administration or a claim against Kandoo, contact the joint administrators.Email: kandoo.queries@kbl-advisory.comKandoo is no longer arranging finance. If you have an existing loan agreement arranged by Kandoo, your agreement is with your lender, not Kandoo. Continue making repayments to your lender as usual. publications.title: Bereaved families need support, not a battle with paperwork
publications.summary: Investment firms must do more to help people dealing with the death of a loved one, after a review found confusing communications, delays and gaps in support. The FCA reviewed how financial advisers, wealth managers and investment platforms support bereaved families and those handling someone’s estate.Some firms provided thoughtful, personal support. Others had processes that risked adding to people’s distress and financial pressure.Some firms left people unclear about what to do next or offered limited ways to get in touch. In some cases, advice fees were still being taken until an original death certificate was provided.Kate Tuckley, head of department, consumer investments at the FCA, said, 'Dealing with someone’s finances after a death should not mean a battle with paperwork. Firms should ease the burden, not add to it.'Families need clear information and help without needless delays

publications.title: Supervision of insurance intermediaries: additional costs to protect clients
publications.summary: To strengthen client protection, over 12,000 insurance intermediaries have been subject to ongoing supervision by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority FINMA since 2024, as required by law. After around three years, the supervisory authority is taking stock: Despite information and prevention campaigns, the problems identified in the intermediary market have so far proved to be more serious than expected. The supervisory levy for untied, registered intermediaries is insufficient to fund the supervisory tasks required by law and is therefore being increased. The new levy will come into force at the beginning of 2027.
